headline: Clean negative. None of the published tactical asset allocation models clears the PROTOCOL section 3 bar in CA, FED or NONE. That covers GEM, Accelerating Dual Momentum, Quint, VAA-G4/G12, DAA, PAA, BAA, HAA, GPM, EAA, FAA, AAA, Faber GTAA-5/13 (+top-k), Ivy, RAA, CDM, plus 60/40, Permanent Portfolio, All-Weather and the other statics: 925 strategy configs in all. The closest unleveraged CA config (3-way GEM with a 5% switching margin) scores +0.03 pp/yr on the full protocol with a 10-year beat rate of 0.49 and boot_p 0.42. Its whole lead was earned in 2000-2010. The faithful models score -1.4 (GEM) to -7.6 (GTAA-5) in CA. Two things sink them: taxes on rotation (relative drag ~0.75 + 0.23 x turnover pp/yr) and a dependence on dodging the 2000-02/2008 crashes. Every finalist trails SPY after 2010, and the pre-2000 holdout is negative. Risk-adjusted, they cut drawdowns (-17..-42% vs SPY -55%), but no TAA model's Sharpe beats SPY's reliably after tax; only static stock/bond mixes do, and those lose on return.
findings: CA (primary), full protocol (95 quarterly starts): the best unleveraged config is GEM3-x-rm5|std (SPY/EFA/EEM 12-month GEM with a 5% switching margin). It scores +0.03, full +0.74, ex10_beat 0.49, ex15_beat 0.47, boot_p 0.42, Sharpe 0.61 vs SPY 0.60 (p=0.51). Sub-periods: 2000-10 +12.85, 2010-20 -5.91, 2020-26 -6.78 pp/yr. Next are ADM13612w-x-rm5 -0.03, ADM-x-mom13612w -0.48 and GEM-x-3way -0.72. The faithful models: GEM -1.39, ADM -1.88, VAA-G4 -1.81, DAA-G4 -1.92, QUINT -2.26, HAA-simple -2.93, GTAA-5 -7.60 (from 2007).
Screen: of 680 distinct non-leveraged CA configs, 2 have a positive score and 0 have a 10-year beat rate >= 0.75. In NONE, 70 of 295 are positive and still 0 reach a 10-year beat rate of 0.75.

Tax drag: across 112 ETF-era configs starting in 2000, (NONE score - CA score) is about 0.75 + 0.23 x turnover pp/yr. 47 of these configs have a positive NONE score, none of them stays positive in CA, and their median drag is 2.6 pp/yr.

Tax-managed execution does not rescue all-or-nothing switchers. The tax1 gain budget freezes them in their last purchase: GEM-x|tax1 was 100% VBMFX in 2001-03 and still 91% bonds in 2026 (CA full -5.04). The lt execution (no short-term gains) helps only high-turnover VAA/GTAA/CDM. VAA-G4-x|lt has a CA full-period excess of +0.72, but its score is -1.61. Over 4 weekly rebalance offsets its CA score averages -3.56, and stricter distribution tax cuts the full-period excess to +0.23.

Regime dependence: every TAA finalist leads SPY by +4.6 to +13.6 pp/yr over 2000-2010 in CA. It then trails by -4.6 to -8.9 over 2010-2020 and by -4.9 to -12.3 over 2020-2026. The ETF-only (-e) versions start after 2003 and are uniformly much worse than the proxy-chain (-x) versions.

Rebalance-day luck is as large as the edge: moving the monthly rebalance to day 8/15/22 shifts screen scores by 1-5 pp/yr. VAA-G4-x scores +1.78 in NONE on day 1 but -2.11 on day 8. ADM-x-mom13612w scores +3.34 in NONE on day 1 but averages +0.66 over 4 offsets; month-end sampling gives -0.35, and its 13612U momentum twin -2.17.

Pre-2000 holdout (Vanguard index-fund versions, long protocol vs VFINX): in CA, GEM ho10 is -2.58, 13612W-ADM -3.96 and ADM -3.64. In NONE they at best tie (GEM +0.01, 13612W-ADM -1.89, ADM -1.59). Their 1986-2026 full-period excess is negative in CA for every model.

Static twins (each finalist's own average mix held statically): timing adds a median +2.9 pp/yr in NONE (15 of 16 positive; VAA-G4 beats its twin in 84% of 10-year windows). In CA it adds a median of only +0.1 pp/yr (range -1.4 to +1.9). The twins are defensive (21-75% bonds) and trail SPY by -0.8 to -3.5 pp/yr in CA.

Risk-adjusted (Sharpe on matched months, stationary bootstrap): no TAA model beats SPY with p <= 0.10 in CA or FED; the best is VAA-G4-x|lt at 0.75 vs 0.60, p=0.31. In NONE the GEM+VAA-G4+ADM blend gets p=0.056 and the DAA canary on SPY p=0.082, which is not significant among ~20 finalists. Static mixes do have a reliable Sharpe edge (60/40 p=0.032 CA / 0.004 NONE; 80/20 tax1 p=0.016 CA), but they trail SPY by 0.9-1.8 pp/yr.

Hindsight (PROTOCOL 5.3): the published menus sit at the 46th-75th percentile of 24 random menus from BROAD_EQUITY_POOL_2003 for each of 5 rules, starting 2005. Almost every random menu also loses (CA medians -4.9 to -7.1). Removing EEM from VAA-G4 drops its NONE score from +1.78 to -0.11 (2000+).

Leverage (labelled): LEV-HAA-S-UPRO|lt (UPRO while the TIP canary is positive, lt execution) scores +6.16 in CA on the full protocol, from 2010-10 only, with boot_p 0.08. It clears criteria 1-3 and fails 4-7. Its Sharpe is 0.77 vs SPY 1.04 on the same months, with 2.1x SPY's vol and a -53% vs -24% monthly drawdown. UPRO buy-and-hold scored +12.79. The same rule with std execution scores -2.54, and on 2x SSO from 2007 +0.47.

Diagnostics: walk-forward selection of the family's best trailing-10y config loses 6-7 pp/yr out of sample in CA and 11-13 in NONE (0 of 3 dates beat SPY). PBO is 0.58-0.77 on the 2000-start subsets, and the DSR of the best non-leveraged CA config is 0.00-0.19.
FED (secondary): the best config is ADM13612w-x-rm5|std at +0.73 score / +1.39 full, but boot_p 0.36 and ex10_beat 0.52, so it fails. ADM-x-mom13612w is +0.24, GEM3-x-rm5 +0.34.

Static allocations never beat SPY on return in any regime: the best is 80/20 at -0.87 CA (full); 60/40 is -1.81, Permanent Portfolio -4.2 and All-Weather -4.9 (screen). Each is also negative in the 1986+ long history.

lab_bugs: Engine/WeightStrategy: the annual tax settlement (backtester/engine.py, 'self.portfolio.cash -= tax') can drive cash negative with no interest charge. With execution='tax', blocked sells leave the debt in place for months: VAA-G4-x|lt in CA has mean cash -0.75%, min -10.6% of equity, and 28% of days below -1%. report.table shows negative avg_cash for many tax configs. This gives tax-managed strategies a small free leverage relative to SPY, which never pays tax before the end. Suggest forcing a sale to cover the tax, or charging margin interest.

metrics.summary: bench_sharpe and bench_max_dd always come from the protocol's first start (2000-01 / 1986-01), even when a config's first valid start is later. In report.table, SPY's -55% drawdown and its 2000-start Sharpe therefore sit next to models that start in 2007-2011. scratch/taa_models/risk.py:matched() recomputes both over matched months.

metrics.walk_forward: step_quarters=4 is applied as an index step over protocol.starts. On yearly-start protocols (screen, long_screen) that is a 4-YEAR step, so a screened grid's 10/5 walk-forward has only 3 decision dates (2012, 2016, 2020) and 5/3 only 4. The criterion-4 diagnostic is very coarse there.

metrics.monthly_matrix(...).dropna() keeps only the months common to ALL configs. A single late-starting config (e.g. one UPRO config starting in 2011) silently truncates PBO and DSR for the whole grid to 2011-2026. A per-config common-start subset (as done here) or pairwise handling would be safer.

`protocol` column; `m_*`/`b_*` columns are matched-period risk statistics of the model and SPY).

Units: excess and score are percentage points of after-tax CAGR per year vs SPY ("+1.00" = 1 pp/yr).
score = mean of the average excess over 5-, 10- and 15-year windows (the lab's pre-registered rank).

## Verdict

**No published tactical asset allocation model, and none of the 925 variants tried, beats
buying and holding SPY after California taxes with good confidence. None clears the PROTOCOL
section 3 bar in CA, FED or NONE.** This is a clean negative for the family.

* **California (primary).** On the full protocol (95 quarterly starts 2000-2023) the closest is
  three-way Global Equities Momentum with a 5% switching margin (`GEM3-x-rm5`: SPY / EFA / EEM by
  12-month return, AGG when SPY trails T-bills): score **+0.03**, full-period excess +0.74, but
  10-year beat rate 0.49, 15-year 0.47, boot_p 0.42, Sharpe 0.61 vs SPY's 0.60 (p = 0.51), and its
  whole lead is 2000-2010 (+12.9 pp/yr; 2010-2020 -5.9, 2020-2026 -6.8). Next: 13612W Accelerating
  Dual Momentum with the same margin (-0.03, the best of its four weekly rebalance offsets, which
  average -1.94) and without it (-0.48), plain 3-way GEM (-0.72). The faithful published models all lose: GEM -1.39, VAA-G4 -1.81, DAA-G4 -1.92, ADM
  -1.88, QUINT -2.26, HAA-simple -2.93, Faber GTAA-5 -7.60 (from 2007), and every G12-universe
  model -5 to -10 pp/yr. Of the 680 distinct non-leveraged configs screened in CA, two have a
  positive score and **none has a 10-year beat rate of 0.75** (the bar); in NONE, 70 of 295 have a
  positive score and none has a 10-year beat rate of 0.75 either.
* **Why: taxes plus regime.** A TAA model rotates (1-8x turnover a year) and realizes gains every
  year, much of them short-term (48.1% in CA), while SPY defers everything to the end. Across the
  112 ETF-era configs starting in 2000, CA costs a model 0.75 + 0.23 x turnover pp/yr of score
  relative to SPY; 47 of them have a positive score untaxed and **none of those 47 stays positive
  in CA** (median drag 2.6 pp/yr). And all of the models' edge is from 2000-2009: in CA every TAA
  finalist leads by +4.6 to +13.6 pp/yr over 2000-2010 and trails by -4.6 to -8.9 over 2010-2020
  and by -4.9 to -12.3 over 2020-2026.
* **Tax-managed execution does not rescue them.** A gain budget (`tax1`, the incumbent preset's
  1%/yr rule) freezes an all-or-nothing switcher in whatever it bought before its gains outgrew the
  budget: GEM went to bonds in 2001 and was still 91% bonds in 2026 (CA full-period excess -5.0).
  Forbidding short-term gains (`lt`) helps only the highest-turnover models (VAA-G4: +0.72 full,
  score -1.61), and that is the luckiest of its rebalance days (averaged over four weekly offsets
  it scores -3.56) and shrinks to +0.23 once bond interest is taxed yearly.
* **FED (secondary).** Best: 13612W-ADM with a 5% margin, +0.73 score, boot_p 0.36, 10-year beat
  0.52. Fails.
* **Tax-deferred (NONE, diagnostic only).** Several models beat SPY on average over 2000-2026
  (13612W-ADM +3.3 / +3.7 with a margin, QUINT in four tranches +2.2, VAA-G4 +1.4, 3-way GEM +1.1
  on the full protocol), but 10-year beat rates are 0.49-0.54, boot_p 0.12-0.37, the family's
  walk-forward selection loses out of sample (-11 pp/yr), and the best results are rebalance-day
  luck: 13612W-ADM scores +3.3 on the 1st of the month and +0.7 averaged over four weekly offsets.
  On random menus from 2006 every rule loses (median -3.9 to -6.6 pp/yr), and the published menus sit
  at the 46th-75th percentile of random menus: the menus were not cherry-picked, the period was
  kind to them (two crashes and the 2003-07 emerging-markets boom in the first decade).
* **Pre-2000 holdout contradicts them.** In windows ending before 2000 the 1986+ Vanguard-fund
  versions lose to VFINX in CA (GEM ho10 -2.58, 13612W-ADM -3.96, ADM -3.64) and at best tie it
  without tax (GEM +0.01, 13612W-ADM -1.89, ADM -1.59); their 1986-2026 full-period excess is
  negative in CA for every model.

  SPY's -55% drawdown to -17..-42%. On matched months, no TAA model's Sharpe ratio beats SPY's with
  bootstrap p <= 0.10 in CA or FED (best: VAA-G4 `lt`, 0.75 vs 0.60, p = 0.31). In NONE two do
  at p < 0.10 (GEM + VAA-G4 + ADM blend, p = 0.056; DAA canary on SPY, p = 0.082), not significant
  among ~20 finalists. The only configs with a reliable Sharpe edge in every regime are static
  stock/bond mixes (60/40 p = 0.03 CA / 0.004 NONE; 80/20 p = 0.02-0.03 CA), which trail SPY on
  return by 0.9-1.8 pp/yr. Versus their own average allocation held statically, the finalists'
  timing adds a median +2.9 pp/yr in NONE (range -1.2 to +5.1; VAA-G4 beats its static twin in 84%
  of 10-year windows) but a median +0.1 pp/yr in CA (range -1.4 to +1.9): the signal is real
  untaxed, and the tax bill takes it.
* **Leverage (labelled).** A 3x S&P fund (UPRO) held while TIP's momentum is positive, with `lt`
  execution, scores +6.16 in CA on the full protocol (starts from 2010-10) with boot_p 0.08 and a
  10-year beat rate of 1.00, i.e. it clears criteria 1-3. It fails 4-7: the family's walk-forward is
  negative, the same rule with standard execution scores -2.54 and on the 2x fund (2007+) +0.47
  (boot_p 0.23), UPRO has existed only in a bull market, and there is no long-history check. Its
  Sharpe ratio is below SPY's over the same months (0.77 vs 1.04), with twice SPY's volatility and a
  -53% vs -24% monthly drawdown; UPRO bought and held scored +12.8, and its own average mix held
  statically (55% UPRO, 45% bills/bonds) +3.7 with a higher Sharpe. It is leverage in a bull market,
  not timing skill.

## What was tested (all of it)

Every model is a target-weight signal run through the lab's `WeightStrategy`, so commission,
slippage, tax lots, the January tax settlement and the terminal liquidation tax are the site's.
Execution variants: `std` (trade to targets on each rebalance), `tax1` (losses always sold, gains
only within 1% of the portfolio per year: the incumbent preset's rule), `lt` (losses always sold,
no short-term gain ever realized, long-term gains unlimited).

Universes and launch dates. `-e` = the published ETFs only; windows start when every ETF and its
12-month signal history exist (2004-2010). `-x` = the same ETFs with an index-mutual-fund proxy
chain before launch (EFA|VGTSX, EEM|VEIEX, AGG|VBMFX, TLT|VUSTX, IEF|VFITX, SHY|VFISX, LQD|VWESX,
HYG|VWEHX, VNQ|IYR|VGSIX, TIP|VIPSX, IWM|NAESX, SCZ|EFA|VGTSX, ...); a chain member that is held
keeps being used, so an ETF launch never forces a taxable switch. `requires`/`min_start` = the
earliest member of every chain plus 400 days of signal history, so no window starts before every
sleeve has an instrument (no "waiting in cash for a launch"). GLD (2004) and DBC/GSG (2006) have no
proxies, so the G12-universe models start in 2008-2009 even with chains. `-L` = mutual funds only,
1986+, benchmark VFINX (long protocols). Momentum is sampled at calendar-month offsets from today's
close (`cal`, default) or at completed month-ends (`me`, the papers' monthly data, traded the next
trading day).

## Concerns and caveats

1. **Negative cash after the January tax settlement (engine).** The engine pays each year's tax
   from cash; a fully invested strategy goes to negative cash (an interest-free loan) until it next
   sells. Standard execution repays it at the next monthly rebalance, but the tax-managed executions
   may not be allowed to sell: `VAA-G4-x|lt` in CA averages -0.75% cash, reaches -10.6% of equity, and
   spends 28% of days below -1%. This flatters tax-managed configs slightly (order of 0.05 pp/yr
   here) relative to SPY, which never pays tax before the end. Reported as a lab issue.
2. **Distributions taxed as deferred gains (PROTOCOL 5.5).** Bond-heavy models are flattered in
   CA/FED; the battery's stricter accounting lowers full-period CA excess by 0.06-0.49 pp/yr. It
   would make every CA conclusion here more negative, not less.
3. **Wash sales.** Standard execution does not enforce the wash-sale rule; TAA models regularly
   sell at a loss in a risk-off month and rebuy within 30 days. Real CA results for `std` configs
   would be slightly worse (deferred loss deductions). `tax1`/`lt` executions have the 31-day guard.
4. **Mutual-fund proxies before ETF launch.** `-x` configs trade Vanguard index funds before the
   ETFs existed (2000-2007). Fund NAVs are total-return like the ETFs, but Vanguard restricts round
   trips within 30 days; monthly switching would occasionally breach that. The `-e` (ETF-only)
   versions start later and are uniformly worse, because they miss 2000-02.
5. **Start-date and rebalance-day sensitivity.** Full-period excess from January 2000 flatters every
   TAA model (it starts at the top of a bubble); the score (5/10/15-year windows) is the fairer
   number and is negative in CA for every model. Moving the monthly rebalance by one to three weeks
   moves scores by 1-5 pp/yr; several "best" configs are the luckiest offset of their rule.
6. **Signal at today's close, trade at today's close** (the lab's convention). With a one-day lag
   the CA scores move by -1.8 to +0.2 pp/yr (VAA-G4 `lt` -1.61 -> -3.45; 13612W-ADM -0.48 -> -0.88,
   with margin -0.03 -> -0.50; 3-way GEM -0.72 -> -0.73, with margin +0.03 -> +0.21): the lag never
   turns a negative CA score into a meaningful positive one, and VAA-G4 (which relies on same-close
   execution) loses most.
7. **Multiple testing.** 925 strategy configs (700 distinct in the CA screen). With that
   many tries a couple of near-zero positive CA scores are expected by chance; the deflated Sharpe
   of the best non-leveraged CA config is 0.00-0.19.
8. **Duplicates.** Some configs are byte-different but behave identically (13612U = avg(1,3,6,12);
   VAA `taxhold` = VAA under `lt`; rel_margin 2% = 5% for VAA under `lt`; `-e`/`-x` statics with
   no chain). They are counted once in the diagnostics (de-duplicated by config content, not by
   behaviour).
9. **Hindsight checks use 2005+ starts** (so every random menu has history); they cannot test the
   2000-02 period, where the published menus did best. Star removal on the full 2000+ windows covers
   VAA-G4 (EEM) and QUINT (QQQ).
10. **Leveraged-fund results** come from 2007+ (SSO) and 2010+ (UPRO) windows only, with no
    long-history proxy in this family.

## Conclusion

For a taxable California account the answer from this family is **no**: none of the published
tactical asset allocation models (GEM, Accelerating Dual Momentum, Quint, VAA, DAA, PAA, BAA, HAA,
GPM, EAA, FAA, AAA, Faber GTAA-5/13 and their aggressive top-k versions, Ivy, Robust Asset
Allocation, Composite Dual Momentum) or the static allocations (60/40, Permanent Portfolio,
All-Weather, Golden Butterfly, Swensen, 3-fund) beats buying and holding SPY after CA tax with
confidence, and neither do the ~900 variants, ensembles, hysteresis / confirmation / tax-hold rules
and tax-managed executions tried. The best unleveraged CA config is a coin flip against SPY (3-way
GEM with a 5% switching margin: score +0.03, 10-year beat 0.49, boot_p 0.42) whose entire lead was
earned in 2000-2010. The incumbent site preset (tax-managed 12-1 momentum over 22 ETFs, CA score
+0.66, boot_p 0.025) is better than anything unleveraged in this family. The one large CA number in
the family (UPRO, a 3x S&P fund, timed by HAA's TIP canary with `lt` execution: +6.16) is leverage
in a 2010-2026 bull market with a lower Sharpe ratio than SPY, and it fails the bar's neighbourhood,
hindsight and walk-forward tests.

What these models genuinely deliver is risk reduction: max drawdowns of -17% to -42% instead of
-55%, and a timing signal that beats a static mix of the same assets by a median 2.9 pp/yr without
tax. In CA most of that timing value goes to taxes (median +0.1 pp/yr left), and the models'
defensive average allocation costs more than that against SPY in rising markets. If the goal is a smaller
drawdown rather than a higher after-tax return, a static stock/bond mix is the statistically
reliable way to buy it in this sample (higher Sharpe than SPY at p = 0.02-0.03 in CA, near-zero
turnover), at a cost of about 0.9 pp/yr (80/20) to 1.8 pp/yr (60/40) of after-tax return. In a
tax-deferred account the dual-momentum and VAA models are plausible risk-reducers with a positive but
statistically unproven return edge that came from one decade.
